name: E. Clarke and Julia Arnold House
by: Frank Lloyd Wright, John H. Howe
key_features: Frank Lloyd Wright's low Usonian house on Columbus's edge, overlooking farmland, built of Wisconsin limestone, redwood and glass.

name: Eden Court Theatre
key_features: 1976 theatre that incorporated the Gothic Bishop's Palace; 2007 extension added a second auditorium.

name: Gobierno Civil de Tarragona
key_features: Competition-winning seat of government in natural stone; about half its area is housing, all furnished by De la Sota.

name: Hamilton City Hall
key_features: Eight-storey International Style city hall, officially opened 21 November 1960.

name: Kreeger Museum
key_features: Philip Johnson's museum in the former Kreeger family home, holding 19th and 20th-century paintings and sculpture.

name: Lanaras Weekend House
key_features: Two thin concrete slabs on slender steel posts, glazed and shuttered between, above stone terrace walls.

name: Lyon Museum of Contemporary Art
key_features: Flexible galleries built behind the kept 1930s facade of the old exhibition hall in the Cité Internationale.

name: Marisfrolg Pavilion
key_features: Biomimetic forms drawn from tropical plants and insect exoskeletons, clad in a mosaic of tile, brick and stone.

name: Nakagawa-machi Bato Hiroshige Museum
key_features: Local cedar louvres cover roof and walls alike, filtering light into galleries lined with washi paper.

name: Nantes Courthouse
key_features: A black grid of slender columns and a vast dark hall give a severe image of justice by the Loire.

name: Narayanhiti Palace Museum
key_features: Royal palace using Nepalese building styles as a national symbol; designed by Benjamin Polk, begun 1963.

name: Nilson Nelson Gymnasium
by: Cláudio Cianciarullo, Ícaro de Castro Mello, Eduardo de Castro Mello
key_features: Indoor arena opened in 1973; a 2008 renovation cut capacity from 24,286 to 11,105 seats.

name: Otaniemi Chapel
key_features: The wall behind the altar is fully glazed onto a forest holding a cross, under a timber truss roof.

name: Palau Sant Jordi
key_features: A domed space-frame roof was assembled on the ground and jacked into place over the Olympic arena.

name: Savill Building
key_features: Three-domed larch gridshell roof on steel quadropods, with a planted green roof over the entrance.

name: Skopje Railway Station
key_features: Tracks raised on a long concrete deck over massive piers, part of Tange's post-earthquake city plan.

name: Taipei Fine Arts Museum
key_features: Grey-white gallery tubes crossing in a 井 (hash) shaped plan, their box-like ends cantilevered out.

name: Tokyo Metropolitan Teien Art Museum
key_features: Former princely residence with French Art Deco rooms, Lalique glass doors and a porcelain perfume fountain.

name: Toronto City Hall
key_features: Two curved office towers cup a saucer-shaped council chamber above a civic square.

name: Torre Latinoamericana
key_features: Steel frame on deep piles through soft lakebed clay, engineered to ride out the city's major earthquakes.

name: Universidad Laboral de Gijón
key_features: Vast stone-and-brick campus planned as a self-contained town around a colonnaded square and a tall tower.

name: Victoria Memorial
key_features: Indo-Saracenic memorial-museum in white Makrana marble, in 26 hectares of gardens, opened in 1921.

name: Yamaguchi Center for Arts and Media (YCAM)
key_features: Arts centre with a contemporary art museum and the city's central library under one roof.

name: Zarya Vostoka building
key_features: Constructivist headquarters of the Russian-language newspaper Zarya Vostoka.

name: 2 Willow Road
key_features: A concrete-framed brick terrace with a spiral stair core and a long first-floor window band.

name: 23 de Enero Superblocks
key_features: Fifteen-storey slab blocks with skip-floor corridors house thousands on the hills above downtown.

name: 78 Derngate
key_features: A Georgian terrace house remodelled with a black hall of stencilled triangles and a stepped rear bay.

name: Aalto House (Riihitie)
key_features: Whitewashed brick and dark timber cladding wrap a house and studio stepped toward the garden.

name: Accordia
by: Feilden Clegg Bradley Studios, Alison Brooks Architects, Maccreanor Lavington
key_features: Dense brick terraces, mews and courtyards set among mature trees; the first housing scheme to win the Stirling Prize.

name: Al Faisaliah Tower
key_features: A tapering tower braced by four corner legs that meet at a glass globe near the top.

name: National Museum and Research Center of Altamira
key_features: Low museum stepping along the hillside, its roofs folding into the slope; it houses a replica of the cave.

name: Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar Memorial Park
key_features: Red sandstone memorial on 108 acres; 124 elephant statues flank the entrance, with an 80-foot pyramid-type structure.

name: Amer Fort
key_features: Red sandstone and marble on four levels, each with a courtyard; Sukh Niwas cooled by water channels.

name: American Air Museum, Duxford
key_features: One long low precast-concrete vault, partly sunk into the ground, with a fully glazed end wall.

name: Anahuacalli Museum
key_features: Pyramid-like museum of dark volcanic stone with mosaic ceilings, drawing on pre-Hispanic temples.

name: Antwerpen-Centraal railway station
key_features: Stone-clad terminal building of 1895-1905; the viaduct into the station is by Jan Van Asperen.

name: Art Gallery of Alberta
key_features: A 190 m stainless steel ribbon swoops through the glazed entry and out over the plaza.

name: Asian Art Museum of San Francisco
key_features: A Beaux-Arts library converted into galleries, its grand stair kept and a top-lit court added.

name: Atakule
key_features: Tower with a revolving restaurant that turns 360 degrees in one hour.

name: Civic Theatre
by: Charles Bohringer and William T. Leighton
key_features: Atmospheric theatre where lighting and decor suggest an open sky with twinkling stars; opened 1929.

name: Austin City Hall
key_features: Designed to reflect the city's vitality; built partly with recycled materials.

name: Baghdad Central Station
key_features: Domed station designed by a Scot who had assisted Lutyens in New Delhi; four platforms.

name: Bagsværd Church
key_features: A plain industrial shell outside; inside, a billowing concrete ceiling washed with daylight.

name: Banyuwangi International Airport
key_features: Low, naturally ventilated terminal under grass-covered roofs, its form drawn from the Osing people's headband.

name: Barbican Centre
key_features: Arts centre buried below a raised podium of walkways, lakes and bush-hammered concrete towers.

name: Basílica del Voto Nacional
key_features: Neo-Gothic basilica up to 83 m high, consecrated 1988, with a viewing platform and the National Pantheon in its crypt.

name: Bauhaus-Archiv
key_features: Shed roofs with curved north-light profiles crown a low white gallery block.

name: Bayard–Condict Building
key_features: Sullivan's only New York building: 12 storeys, Chicago School, with a terracotta facade.

name: Beira railway station
by: Paulo de Melo Sampaio, Francisco Castro
key_features: Tropical modernist station: a long concrete concourse below a tower block, with shaded facades.

name: Benedictine Monastery Chapel
key_features: Two interlocked white masonry cubes, rotated against each other, lit by hidden slots of indirect light.

name: Bergisel Ski Jump
key_features: A concrete tower carries a café and ramp that merge into one continuous, flowing form.

name: Berlin Musical Instrument Museum
by: Edgar Wisniewski, after designs by Hans Scharoun
key_features: Scharoun's open, terraced museum landscape of stairs and galleries, beside his Philharmonie at the Kulturforum.

name: Berlin State Library (Haus Potsdamer Straße)
key_features: Terraced reading platforms flow through one vast hall lit from above by many skylights.

name: Biltmore House
by: Richard Morris Hunt (house); Frederick Law Olmsted (landscape)
key_features: Chateauesque house of Indiana limestone with Guastavino tile vaulting; the largest private house in the US.

name: Blanton Museum of Art
key_features: Michener Gallery Building opened 2006; Snohetta's 2023 plaza adds twelve three-story shade petals.

name: Blauwe Theehuis
key_features: Two stacked circular floors under a circular roof 'saucer'; concrete, steel and glass, with blue-painted pillars.

name: BMW Central Building
key_features: Cascading office floors sit under an overhead conveyor carrying car bodies through the open workspace.

name: Bourse de Commerce - Pinault Collection
by: Henri Blondel (1889 rebuild); Tadao Ando (2021 conversion)
key_features: 18th-century rotunda reopened in 2021 with a Tadao Ando concrete cylinder inside it as main gallery.

name: Buffalo City Court Building
key_features: Ten-storey courthouse on Niagara Square, next to Buffalo City Hall.

name: Cairo Opera House
key_features: A gift from Japan to Egypt, built 1985-88 to give Cairo a new opera house after the Khedivial Opera.

name: Camino Real Hotel, Mexico City
key_features: Magenta lattice wall screens a sequence of courtyards and pools from the street.

name: Çanakkale Martyrs' Memorial
by: Doğan Erginbaş, İsmail Utkular, Ertuğrul Barla
key_features: Four 7.5 m square columns carry a 25 by 25 m concrete slab.

name: Casa delle Armi
key_features: Luigi Moretti's experimental Casa del Balilla, designed in 1934 and finished in 1936 as a fencing academy.

name: Casa Rozes
key_features: Coderch's 1961–62 clifftop house, stepped down in cube-like levels beneath a cantilevered terrace.

name: Cathedral of Christ the Light
key_features: Glulam timber ribs and glass louvres form a vesica-shaped shell of light above a concrete base.

name: Cathedral of Maringá
key_features: Cone-shaped, 124 m tall, reportedly inspired by Sputnik; among the tallest churches in the Americas.

name: Central Government Complex, Tamar
key_features: Two towers joined at the top to frame a giant open door, with a park running through to the harbour.

name: Central Hall, University of York
by: Robert Matthew, Johnson-Marshall & Partners (design by John Speight)
key_features: Brutalist examination and lecture hall whose cantilevers let it stand out gently from its surroundings.

name: Central Library, Central University of Venezuela
key_features: Main library of the Central University of Venezuela, inaugurated 1953.

name: Chiesa del Santo Volto
key_features: Seven towers ring a central church; an old steelworks chimney becomes its bell tower.

name: Chikatsu Asuka Museum
key_features: The roof is a vast stepped concrete stair for viewing the surrounding ancient burial mounds.

name: Children's Memorial, Yad Vashem
key_features: An underground hollow where a few candles, reflected by mirrors, multiply into endless points of light.

name: Church of Cristo Obrero
key_features: Undulating reinforced brick walls rise into a roof of thin, wave-like brick vaults.

name: Church of Saint Peter, Durazno
key_features: Reinforced-brick walls and a folded brick roof spanning the nave without columns.

name: Church of St Aengus, Burt
key_features: Church voted Ireland's building of the 20th century in a 1999 RIAI readers' poll.

name: Class of 1959 Chapel
key_features: Non-denominational chapel at Harvard Business School, part of a master plan complementing the 1927 campus.

name: County Hall, Cork
key_features: 17-storey council office block; its original concrete facade was replaced by louvered glass cladding.

name: Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum
key_features: Plan forms a bass clef; a sweeping arch evokes a 1959 Cadillac fin; front windows echo piano keys.

name: Croatian National Theatre
key_features: Landmark theatre with a bright yellow façade by the Viennese firm Fellner & Helmer; built 1894–95.

name: Cummins Corporate Office Building
key_features: Built around the Cerealine Building, Cummins' first factory building, on an old railroad yard.

name: Davenport Public Library
key_features: Main Library housed in a 1960s building by the architect of the Kennedy Center.

name: de Young Museum
key_features: A perforated, dimpled copper skin wraps low galleries and a twisting tower in Golden Gate Park.

name: Denys Wilkinson Building
key_features: Large fan-shaped superstructure built to house a Van de Graaff generator.

name: Diehtosiida
key_features: A Sámi academic campus in Kautokeino housing the Sámi University College, Sámi Archives and other institutions; opened 2009.

name: Doha Tower
key_features: A cylindrical tower behind layered aluminium mashrabiya screens, carried on a diagonal grid of columns.

name: Dokk1
by: Schmidt Hammer Lassen Architects, Kristine Jensen
key_features: Polygonal library and citizens' hall on a harbour pier: a glass box under a wide overhanging upper floor.

name: Dominican Chapel, Ibadan
key_features: Thick walls, a shaded ambulatory and carved timber details keep the chapel cool and dim.

name: Avianca Building
by: Esguerra, Sáenz, Urdaneta, Samper y Cía., with Ricaurte Prieto Carrizosa
key_features: 40-storey office tower on Parque Santander, Colombia's tallest building when finished in 1969.

name: Figge Art Museum
key_features: 115,000 sq ft museum on the Mississippi, designed by David Chipperfield; opened August 2005.

name: Galleria Department Store (West)
key_features: A blind 1970s concrete box re-clad in 4,330 glass discs that shift colour by day and glow with LEDs by night.

name: Grande Poste d'Alger
key_features: Neo-Moorish central post office, Algeria's largest; arcaded facade; a museum since 2015.

name: Guaranty Building (Prudential Building)
key_features: An early skyscraper and National Historic Landmark.

name: Gyumri railway station
key_features: Soviet Armenian modernist hall whose spatial composition echoes medieval Armenian architecture.

name: Haus Freudenberg
key_features: Hermann Muthesius's Berlin-Nikolassee house for Hermann Freudenberg, now under monument protection.

name: Hospital Naval Pedro Mallo
key_features: Testa's sculptural concrete hospital on the edge of Parque Centenario, often read as a moored ship.

name: House of Wisdom
key_features: A thin floating roof overhangs the two-storey glass library by 15 m on every side, shading it from the desert sun.

name: Houston Astrodome
by: Hermon Lloyd & W. B. Morgan; Wilson, Morris, Crain & Anderson; Praeger-Kavanagh-Waterbury
key_features: Dome about 710 ft across with Lucite roof panes; first major venue to install artificial turf (1966).

name: Kaédi Regional Hospital
key_features: Hospital of hand-fired local brick built as a sequence of domes and vaults, cooled and lit without machines.

name: MADRE Museum
key_features: Siza adapted the Palazzo Donnaregina over four floors; a roof terrace carries Paladino's sculpture Cavallo.

name: Mivtachim Sanitarium (ELMA Arts Complex and Hotel)
key_features: Brutalist retreat for workers, designed 1966 and completed 1969; later reopened as the ELMA hotel.
